metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: If no resource is specified in the authorization/token request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific tests must not flag opaque-token issuance as a bug; it is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions may not appear through refresh if they were not part of the original requested scope set; a new authorization flow is required.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing expanded scopes after refresh is by design, not under-granting or over-granting.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not fetched directly from the authorization code flow; they are obtained via refresh token flow or client credentials with organization parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: A missing organization token in the initial code exchange is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify already issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated permissions.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid false positives when old tokens continue to authorize until expiration.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs retain their original scopes after role or permission changes until they expire.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect permission reductions or expansions.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission or role changes do not modify existing JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect the updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag old tokens retaining old scopes until expiry as stale-cache vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in fails because the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: Fallback is expected and should not be treated as a broken flow.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing users signing in with enterprise SSO are automatically linked to the existing Logto account when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merge on matching email is documented behavior and can look like cross-user collapse if tests ignore email-linking semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Ending the centralized Logto session does not revoke grants that have offline_access; related refresh capability can remain until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token refresh success in this case is by design, not necessarily a revocation flaw.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource or organization context is requested, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat inability to locally validate such a token as a JWT-validation bug; use introspection or /oidc/me semantics instead.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource or organization context is requested, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific tests must not treat opaque-token behavior as a JWT validation bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For JWT-format access tokens, the fuzzer MUST request a specific API resource (`resource`) and/or organization context as documented. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. JWT-focused tests for oidc_jwt must therefore include `resource` (or organization token parameters) so the returned `access_token` is actually a JWT rather than an opaque token.

When testing I1 issuer validation and trust-anchor behavior, the verifier MUST validate `iss` against the tenant issuer `https://<tenant>/oidc` and fetch keys from `/oidc/jwks` or discovery. Do not treat issuer as optional: the docs explicitly require issuer validation and Logto does not support customizing issuer/JWKS URI.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST configure and validate audience manually against the API resource indicator. The example validators set `verify_aud` / `ValidateAudience` to false in JWT libraries and require application code to check `aud` against the registered API resource or organization audience. A token lacking the expected audience must be treated as invalid by the test oracle, not as a platform bypass.

`resource` matching is EXACT string match only. The docs state the `resource` parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). For multi-resource or wildcard-style tests, do NOT use wildcard patterns; `*` is not a matcher. Use the exact registered URI or omit `resource` only when intentionally testing opaque-token/default-audience behavior.

Scope/permission names are EXACT string match only. Logto documentation explicitly says scope names must exactly match permission names defined on the API resource; prefixes or shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For multi-identity or broad-match tests, do NOT set scope to wildcard-like values; request the exact permission strings.

For I2 expired/future token tests, include a CONTROL token request/login in the same scenario using a valid token configuration. Otherwise, a rejection may be caused by missing `resource`, wrong audience, or wrong organization context rather than freshness enforcement.

Organization tokens cannot be obtained directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization-scoped JWTs, first obtain a refresh token (or use client credentials), then call `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` or `grant_type=client_credentials` plus `organization_id` (and `resource` for org API resources). Do not expect the initial authorization-code token response to directly contain an organization token.

For organization-level API tests, `organization_id` changes authorization semantics. Without `organization_id`, only global roles/permissions are evaluated; with `organization_id`, Logto evaluates organization roles and emits `organization_id` in the JWT. The fuzzer MUST include and vary `organization_id` deliberately when testing org-bound authorization.

Global permission enlargement is not reflected by refresh unless the scopes were part of the original authorization request. For I3 permission-change tests on global API resources, a new OAuth authorization flow is required to obtain newly enlarged scopes not originally requested. Do not treat absence of newly granted scopes after refresh as a stale-cache bug if the original request did not include them.

Permission reductions are only reflected in newly issued JWTs; existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. For I3 config-tightening or permission-tightening tests, compare a pre-change token with a NEWLY issued post-change token. Do not expect already-issued JWTs to be retroactively narrowed.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected setup errors rather than security behavior.

For token exchange tests, `session_token` must always be the returned `access_token`, never `id_token`. Logto docs distinguish access tokens as the bearer credential for APIs and userinfo; using `id_token` as the session credential will produce invalid results.

For PAT-based token exchange, `subject_token_type` must be exactly `urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token`. For impersonation/subject-token exchange, use the documented access-token token type values. Do not mix token-type URNs across exchange scenarios or interpret resulting errors as audience/authorization failures.

Current Logto SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out of the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` are not revoked by end-session and may remain valid until grant TTL expiry (default 180 days). For I2/session-revocation tests, revoking browser session alone is insufficient to prove refresh-token invalidation; explicitly test token revocation or grant expiry separately.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. Do not assume omitted or zero-like UI state means literal zero lifetime. Treat the documented default as nonzero and explicitly configure short lifetimes when testing expiry behavior.

Numeric sentinel analysis: organization/member magic-link one-time tokens default to 10 minutes if `expiresIn` is not specified. Do not assume omission means immediate expiry or disabled expiry. Use explicit short values when testing freshness boundaries.

For direct sign-in tests using `direct_sign_in`, failure to find or enable the connector falls back to the standard sign-in page by design. Do not interpret fallback to the hosted sign-in page as a flow-coherence or auth-bypass issue.

For OIDC auth-flow tests involving `ui_locales`, `first_screen`, `identifier`, or `login_hint`, these parameters only affect the current interaction and UI/email behavior; they do not permanently change tenant settings or authorization state. Do not treat differences caused by these parameters as identity or authorization confusion.

Logto issues JWT access tokens for API resources only when a specific resource or organization context is requested. If no resource is specified, the access token is opaque and intended for /oidc/me or introspection. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT validation, the fuzzer MUST request a resource (or organization token context) during authorization or token exchange; otherwise failures may be due to opaque-token issuance rather than JWT validation.

For I1 issuer-validation and trust-anchor tests, the verifier MUST validate issuer against the tenant issuer from discovery or the fixed pattern https://<tenant>/oidc, and MUST fetch keys from /oidc/jwks or discovery jwks_uri. Do not treat issuer or JWKS URI as configurable per application; Logto documentation states they are tenant-fixed.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). Do not use prefixes, shortened forms, or wildcard assumptions. A mismatched resource causes token audience mismatch by design.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names must exactly match permission names defined for the API resource. Wildcards and prefixes are not supported. If testing multiple permissions, request the exact full scope strings.

For I5 empty_audience and default-audience tests, Logto has a by-design default API resource behavior. If a default API resource is configured, omitting resource can still yield a JWT for that default audience; if openid is included with no resource, Logto may issue an opaque token for userinfo instead. The fuzzer MUST record whether a default API resource is configured before interpreting omitted-resource behavior as an audience-binding flaw.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not retroactively modified. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens. A valid coherence test must compare newly issued tokens after config change, not reuse an old token and expect its claims to shrink or grow.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh does NOT add newly granted scopes unless they were part of the original authorization request set; obtaining scopes outside the original request requires a new authorization flow. Do not flag missing newly granted scopes after refresh as a bug unless the scopes were originally requested.

For organization-token tests, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token via authorization_code, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters, or use client_credentials with organization parameters. Treat direct auth-code organization-token absence as by design.

For I5 organization-binding tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization permissions or organization-level API resources.

For I5 mixed-scope tests, organization permissions and global API permissions are distinct models and cannot be mixed into one organization token expectation. The fuzzer MUST not interpret absence of global API permissions from an organization token as a bug.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running token_exchange tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected behavior.

For token_exchange tests, Logto uses the standard /oidc/token endpoint with application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. The fuzzer MUST send grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and the correct subject_token_type for the token being exchanged (e.g. urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token for PAT).

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer access tokens, do NOT flag replay as a vulnerability by default. Logto documents JWT access tokens as standard bearer tokens and does not document jti replay tracking for ordinary JWT auth. Reuse of the same JWT is expected stateless behavior unless a special one-time subject token flow is under test.

For impersonation token-exchange tests, the subject token returned by the Management API is short-lived and one-time-use, and the resulting impersonation access token does not include a refresh token. Reusing the subject token or expecting refresh semantics on the exchanged token is incorrect test setup.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control request using a valid token in the same environment. Logto examples validate exp and issuer in standard JWT libraries, while audience may be checked manually by the API. Without a control, a 401 may reflect broken verifier setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For sign-out and revocation tests, revoking a token at /oidc/token/revocation or ending the Logto session does not imply all previously issued JWTs instantly become unusable at resource servers unless those servers introspect or otherwise check revocation. Existing JWTs remain valid until expiry by design; only newly issued tokens and centralized session behavior change immediately.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time has documented default 3600 seconds when unset. Omission selects a nonzero platform default rather than literal zero. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume missing/zero-like configuration means immediate expiry; use explicit timing claims in tokens and explicit resource settings where available.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Logto examples show JWT validator clock skew defaults in some framework examples (e.g. .NET example uses 5 minutes), but this is verifier-side sample code, not a Logto server setting. The fuzzer MUST NOT infer a platform-wide leeway sentinel or server-side grace period from these examples.

For global API resource tests, the resource parameter MUST exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator. There is no wildcard or prefix matching. If the fuzzer sends a near-match audience, rejection is expected and not an I5 bug.
Scope names must exactly match permission names defined on the API resource. Prefixes or shortened names are not wildcards. For I5 tests, do not treat partial scope names as equivalent permissions.

When testing organization-level API resources, organization RBAC is applied only if organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id for organization-context authorization tests.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. To obtain an organization token after interactive login, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Do not expect the initial code exchange to directly return an organization token.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected configuration errors rather than security behavior.
For PAT-based token exchange, subject_token_type MUST be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. Using another subject_token_type changes the semantics and invalidates the test.

For impersonation-style token exchange with actor attribution, actor_token must itself be a valid access token and should include openid scope to populate the act claim. Absence of act in that case is configuration-dependent; do not flag missing act unless actor_token was supplied correctly.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued tokens, include a control request using a valid token in the same setup. Otherwise a 401 on the attack token may be caused by wrong issuer, audience, or resource setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Logto validation guidance explicitly verifies issuer and expiration, but audience validation is permission-model dependent and often performed manually by the resource server. For I1/I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish IdP issuance behavior from API-side validation behavior; a token accepted by /oidc/me does not prove it is valid for a custom API audience.

Default API resource behavior is special: if a default API resource is configured and resource is omitted, Logto may issue a JWT for that default audience; if openid is included with no resource, Logto may issue an opaque token for userinfo. The fuzzer MUST explicitly set resource in JWT audience tests instead of relying on tenant defaults.

Permission changes are reflected only in newly issued JWTs; existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. For I3 config-change or permission-tightening tests, the fuzzer MUST obtain a NEW token after the change and MUST NOT expect already-issued JWTs to shrink in place.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the originally requested scope set; a new authorization flow may be required. Do not flag missing newly granted scopes after refresh as a bug unless they were requested in the original authorization.

For organization tokens, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but still only within the originally requested scope set. I5 scope-escalation tests must compare against original requested scopes, not merely current role assignments.

Logto current SDK sign-out flow performs global end-session behavior. However, if offline_access was granted, end-session does not revoke the app grant by default; refresh-token-backed authorization may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. Do not treat successful token refresh after browser sign-out as an automatic I2/I3 violation when offline_access is present.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration default is 3600 seconds when not configured. The docs do not define a special numeric sentinel such as 0 or -1 to disable or inherit behavior. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables expiry or means immediate expiration; use explicit time-based JWT claims like exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and exp={{now_epoch_minus_7200}} for freshness tests.

Grant lifetime after sign-out with offline_access is long-lived by design (default grant TTL 180 days). Tests that expect immediate invalidation of refresh-derived access after end-session will produce false positives unless the grant is explicitly revoked or offline_access is absent.
